This is what Allah promised the believers: the victory of His religion, the elevation of His word, and the humiliation of their enemies among the polytheists, who drove the Messenger and those with him out of Mecca, from the Sacred House of Allah, and expelled them from the land of the Hijaz, over which they had held dominion. Allah gave victory to His Messenger and the believers until he conquered Mecca, humbled the polytheists, and the rule and dominance over those lands passed to the believers. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded his muezzin to proclaim on the Day of the Greater Hajj, which is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), at the time when people gathered, both Muslim and disbelieving, from all of the Arabian Peninsula (Jazirat al-Arab), that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation to the polytheists. Therefore they have no covenant or pact with him; wherever they are found, they shall be killed. It was also said to them: "Do not approach the Sacred Mosque after this your year." That was in the ninth year after the Hijra. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu) led the people in Hajj, and ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu), the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), proclaimed the declaration of disavowal (Bara'ah) on the Day of Sacrifice.

Then the Most High encouraged the polytheists to repent and warned them against persisting in polytheism, saying: ﴿So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you will not cause Allah to fail [to overtake you].﴾ That is, you will not escape Him; rather, you are in His grip, and He is able to set His believing servants against you. ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾ That is, a painful, severe torment in this world through killing, captivity, and expulsion, and in the Hereafter through the Fire, and wretched is the abode.

{4} That is: this complete and absolute disavowal applies to all the polytheists, **except** {those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists} who have remained faithful to their covenant and have committed nothing that would require its annulment, neither diminishing anything from you nor aiding anyone against you. Fulfil their covenant to them until its term, whether short or long, because Islam does not command treachery; it commands fidelity. {Indeed, Allah loves the muttaqin (the God-conscious)}: those who carry out what they were commanded and who guard against polytheism, treachery, and other sins.

{5} Allah says: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed﴾; that is, those in which fighting against the polytheists who have treaties was forbidden, and these are the four months of travel (ash-tasyir al-arba'a), and the full term for whoever has a term longer than them; thus their covenant of protection is cancelled. ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾: in any place and at any time, ﴿and take them captive﴾, ﴿and besiege them﴾; that is, constrict them, so do not let them expand throughout the lands of Allah and His earth which Allah made a place of worship for His servants. These people are not fit to dwell in it, and they do not deserve a single span of it, because the earth is the earth of Allah, and they are His enemies who oppose Him and His messengers, the combatants who wish that the earth be emptied of His religion, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it. ﴿And sit in ambush for them at every place of ambush﴾; that is, every mountain pass and place they pass through. Stand guard in your jihad against them, exert your utmost effort in that, and do not cease in this matter until they repent from their polytheism. Therefore He said: ﴿But if they repent﴾: from their polytheism, ﴿and establish prayer﴾; that is, perform it with its rights, ﴿and give zakah﴾: to its deserving recipients, ﴿then let them go on their way﴾; that is, leave them alone, and let them be like you: for them what is yours, and upon them what is upon you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He forgives shirk and what is less than it for those who repent, and shows them mercy by enabling them to repent and then accepting it from them.

In this verse is evidence that whoever refrains from performing prayer or zakah is to be fought until he pays it, as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) used this as evidence.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 9, verse 6:

﴿6﴾ Since what preceded in His saying, ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and capture them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, was a general command covering all circumstances and every individual among them, the Exalted mentioned that when the public interest requires bringing some of them near, it is permissible, indeed obligatory. So He said: ﴿And if anyone among the polytheists seeks your protection﴾; that is, asks you to grant him protection and to shield him from harm, so that he may hear the words of Allah and observe the state of Islam. ﴿Then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah.﴾ Then, if he embraces Islam, that is well; otherwise, ﴿convey him to his place of safety﴾; that is, the place where he is secure.

The reason for this is that the disbelievers are a people who do not know. Their persistence in disbelief may stem from ignorance, and once that ignorance is removed they may choose Islam over it. Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger, and his community, who follow his example in rulings, to grant protection to whoever asks to hear the words of Allah.

In this there is a clear proof for the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a (the adherents of the Sunna and the main body of the community), who hold that the Qur'an is the uncreated speech of Allah, because He is the one who speaks it, and He attributed it to Himself as the attribute is attributed to the one it describes. It also refutes the doctrine of the Mu'tazila (a rationalist theological school) and those who adopt their view that the Qur'an is created. There are many proofs demonstrating the falsehood of this view, but this is not the place to mention them!

He says: {How can there be for the polytheists a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger}? Have they fulfilled the obligation of faith? Or have they refrained from harming the Messenger of Allah and the believers? Did they not wage war against the truth and support falsehood?! Did they not spread corruption in the land?! It is therefore right that Allah disavow them, and that there be for them no covenant with Him or with His Messenger. {Except those with whom you made a covenant}: from among the polytheists {at al-Masjid al-Haram}: for they have, in the covenant, especially in this noble place, a sanctity that requires that it be observed. {So as long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous}.

Allah, Exalted is He, says to His believing servants, after commanding them to strive (jihad): {Or do you think that you would be left [alone] without Allah having made evident those of you who strive and have not taken other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as intimate friends (waliyjah)?}: that is, without being tested and examined, and without being commanded in a way that distinguishes the truthful from the liar. {And Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive}; that is, He has not yet made manifest knowledge of what is in potential brought out into actuality, so that reward and punishment may be based upon it, and so that He knows those who strive in His cause to raise high His word. {And have not taken other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as intimate friends (waliyjah)}; that is, a friend from among the disbelievers. Rather, they take Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as their allies. So Allah legislated jihad so that this supreme objective might be achieved, namely that the truthful, who show partisanship only to the religion of Allah, be distinguished from the liars who claim faith while they take intimate friends and allies other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. {And Allah is Acquainted with what you do}; that is, He knows what comes to be from you and what proceeds from you, so He tests you in a way that reveals the reality of what you are, and He will recompense you for your deeds, good and bad.

{17} Allah the Exalted says: {It is not for the polytheists} — i.e., it is not fitting or proper — {to maintain the mosques of Allah} through worship, prayer, and other kinds of obedience, while they bear witness against themselves to their own disbelief, as evidenced by their state, their innate nature (fitrah), and the knowledge that many of them have that they are upon disbelief and falsehood. {19} When some of the Muslims, or some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, disagreed about which was superior: the building up (ʿimarah) of the Sacred Mosque through construction, prayer and worship within it, and the provision of water to the pilgrims (siqayat al-hajj), compared with faith in God and striving in His way (jihad), God, exalted is He, informed of the disparity between them, saying: ﴿Do you consider the giving of water to the pilgrims and the building up of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God.﴾ That is: "giving them water from Zamzam," as is well known when this name is used alone, is what is meant. Faith in God and jihad are superior to the provision of water to the pilgrims and the building up of the Sacred Mosque by many degrees, because faith is the root of the religion, by which deeds are accepted and good qualities flourish. As for striving in the way of God, it is the peak of the hump of religion (dhirwat sanam al-din), by which the Islamic religion is preserved and expands, the truth is supported and falsehood is forsaken. As for the building up of the Sacred Mosque and the provision of water to the pilgrims, although they are righteous deeds, they depend upon faith, and they do not contain the benefits that faith and jihad contain. Therefore He said: ﴿They are not equal in the sight of God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ That is: those whose description is wrongdoing, who are not fit to accept anything of good, and for whom nothing but evil is becoming.

{20} Then He stated the excellence explicitly, saying: ﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of God with their wealth and their selves are greater in rank in the sight of God, and it is they who are the triumphant.﴾ "With their wealth": by spending in jihad and equipping the warriors. "And their selves": by going forth with their persons. "Are greater in rank in the sight of God": that is, no one attains what is sought, nor is saved from what is feared, except one who is characterized by their attributes and adorned with their character.

"And gardens for them wherein is enduring bliss": of everything the souls desire and the eyes delight in, of which only God, exalted is He, knows the description and the measure. Among it is that God prepared for those who strive in His way one hundred degrees, between each two degrees is as the distance between the heaven and the earth, and if all creation were gathered in a single one of them, it would suffice them.

{23} God, exalted is He, says: "O you who have believed" — act in accordance with the requirements of faith, by allying yourselves with those who uphold it and being hostile to those who do not. "Do not take your fathers and your brothers" — who are the closest people to you — "and other than them is more so and more fitting" — "as allies if they prefer" — that is, choose — "disbelief over faith. And whoever of you allies with them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers" — because they have dared to disobey Allah and have taken the enemies of Allah as allies. The root of wilayah (allegiance) is love and support, and taking them as allies necessitates giving precedence to their obedience over the obedience of Allah, and to love for them over love for Allah and His Messenger.

{24} For this reason He mentions the cause that necessitates it, which is that the love of Allah and His Messenger must be given precedence over the love of everything else, and all other things must be made subordinate to them. So He says: "Say: If your fathers" — and likewise the mothers — "and your brothers" — by lineage and companionship — "and your spouses and your kindred" — that is, your relatives in general — "and wealth which you have acquired" — that is, which you have earned and exerted yourselves to obtain. He singled it out for mention because it is more cherished by its owners, and its owner is more eager to keep it than one to whom wealth comes without toil or hardship. "And commerce, the slackness of which you fear" — that is, its lack of profit and its decline. This includes all types of trade and gain, such as merchandise of every kind: currency, utensils, weapons, goods, grains, crops, livestock, and other things. "And dwellings with which you are pleased" — because of their beauty, their adornment, and their suitability to your desires. If these things are "dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause," then you are "defiant transgressors," "so wait" — that is, await what punishment will befall you — "until Allah brings His command," which cannot be averted. "And Allah does not guide the defiant people" — that is, those who depart from the obedience of Allah and place something of the aforementioned above the love of Allah.

This noble verse is the greatest proof of the obligation to love Allah and His Messenger, of giving them precedence over the love of everything else, and of the severe warning and the strong abhorrence directed at anyone for whom any of the aforementioned things is dearer than Allah, His Messenger, and striving in His cause. The sign of this is that when two matters are presented to him: one is loved by Allah and His Messenger and has no personal desire in it for himself; and the other is loved by his soul and he desires it, but it causes him to forfeit or diminish something beloved to Allah and His Messenger. If he prefers what his soul desires over what Allah loves, this shows that he is a wrongdoer who has abandoned what is obligatory upon him.

Exalted is He, He bestows favor upon His believing servants by granting them victory in many places of encounter and sites of battle and combat, including on the day of Hunayn, when the hardship weighed heavily upon them and they saw such cowardice and flight that the earth, despite its vastness and breadth, seemed constricted to them. This was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he heard that Hawazin had gathered to fight him. So he (ﷺ) set out toward them with his companions who had conquered Makkah, along with those of the Tulaqa' (the freed ones) of the people of Makkah who had embraced Islam. They numbered twelve thousand, while the polytheists were four thousand. Some of the Muslims were impressed by their numbers, and some of them said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." When they met Hawazin, the latter charged the Muslims in a single assault, and they fled, not turning back for anyone. Only about a hundred men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who stood firm with him, and they began fighting the polytheists. The Prophet (ﷺ) urged his mule forward toward the polytheists, saying: "I am the Prophet, there is no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib." When he saw what the Muslims were doing, he ordered al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who had a loud voice, to call out to the Ansar and the rest of the Muslims. He called out: "O companions of the tree (of Bay'at al-Ridwan)! O people of Surat al-Baqarah!" When they heard his voice, they turned back as one man, engaged in battle with the polytheists, and Allah routed the polytheists in a shameful defeat, and they seized their camp, their women, and their wealth.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 25–27:

{25} This is referring to His saying, ﴿Allah has already given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn﴾. Hunayn is the name of the place where the battle took place between Makkah and al-Ta'if. ﴿When your great number pleased you, but it availed you nothing﴾; that is, it did not benefit you in the least, whether little or much. ﴿And the earth, for all its vastness, closed in on you﴾; because of the distress and grief that afflicted you when you fled. ﴿Then you turned back in retreat﴾; that is, fleeing in defeat.

{26} ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾. Sakinah (tranquility) is that which Allah places in the hearts at times of turmoil, upheaval and terrifying events, by which He steadies them, calms them and makes them content. It is one of the great blessings of Allah upon His servants. ﴿And He sent down hosts you did not see﴾; these were the angels, whom Allah sent as aid to the Muslims on the day of Hunayn, to steady them and to give them the good news of victory. ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾; with defeat, killing, and the Muslims' seizure of their women, children and property. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾; Allah punishes them in this world, and then in the Hereafter He returns them to a severe punishment.

{27} ﴿Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills﴾. Allah did turn in forgiveness to many of those upon whom the battle had fallen; they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) as Muslims, repentant, and he returned to them their women and children. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾; that is, possessor of vast forgiveness and all-encompassing mercy, who pardons great sins for those who repent, shows them mercy by granting them success in repentance, obedience and pardon for their offenses, and accepts their repentance. So let no one despair of His mercy and forgiveness, however great the sins and crimes he has committed.

Ibn Sa'di, Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman, on Surah 9, verse 28:

{28} Allah, exalted is He, says: {O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists} (who associate others in worship with Allah) {are impure} (najas); that is, they are corrupt (khaba'ith) in their beliefs and their deeds. And what impurity is more severe than that of one who worships alongside Allah gods that neither benefit nor harm, nor avail him anything? And their deeds consist of warring against Allah, barring from the way of Allah, supporting falsehood, rejecting the truth, and working corruption on earth rather than righteousness! So it is incumbent upon you to purify the most noble and purest of houses from them. {So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year} (i.e., the year nine after the Hijrah), when Abu Bakr al-Siddiq led the pilgrims in Hajj, and the Prophet (ﷺ) sent his cousin 'Ali to proclaim the declaration (bara'ah) on the Day of the Greater Hajj. He proclaimed that no polytheist may perform Hajj after this year, and no one circumambulates the House naked.

The intended meaning here is not physical impurity, for the disbeliever, like others, is physically pure. This is shown by the fact that Allah permitted marriage with and physical contact with a woman of the People of the Book, and did not command washing what had touched her; and the Muslims continued to come into contact with the bodies of disbelievers, and it is not reported that they were repulsed by them as they are repulsed by impurities. Rather, what is meant, as has been mentioned, is their spiritual impurity through shirk; just as tawhid and faith are purity, shirk is impurity.

And His saying: {And if you fear poverty} (ʿaylah), O Muslims, that is, destitution and need resulting from preventing the polytheists from approaching al-Masjid al-Haram, through the severing of the worldly ties between you and them, {then Allah will enrich you from His bounty}. Provision is not confined to a single door or a single place; rather, no door closes except that many other doors open. For Allah's bounty is vast and His generosity is great, especially for one who gives up something for the sake of the Generous. Indeed Allah is the most generous of the generous, and Allah has fulfilled His promise: He enriched the Muslims from His bounty and spread provision for them such that they became among the greatest of the wealthy and the kings. And His saying: {if He wills} makes the enrichment conditional upon His will, because worldly wealth is not a necessary consequence of faith, nor does it indicate Allah's love; for this reason Allah made it conditional upon His will. Allah gives the world to those whom He loves and those whom He does not love, but He gives faith and religion only to those whom He loves. {Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise}; that is, His knowledge is vast; He knows who deserves wealth and who does not, and He places things in their proper places and situates them in their proper stations.

This noble verse, His saying {So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year}, indicates that the polytheists, who had formerly been the rulers and leaders regarding the House, then after the conquest (of Makkah) the authority came to the Messenger of Allah and the believers, while the polytheists remained in the House and in the honored city of Makkah; then this verse was revealed. And when the Prophet (ﷺ) died, he commanded that they be expelled from the Hijaz, so that no two religions remain in it. All of this is due to the prohibition on every disbeliever coming near al-Masjid al-Haram, and so it falls under His saying: {So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year}.

{29} This verse is a command to fight the disbelievers among the Jews and Christians who {do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day}, in a sound belief that is confirmed by their deeds and actions, {nor do they forbid what Allah has forbidden}, meaning they do not follow His law regarding the prohibition of what is forbidden, {nor adopt the religion of truth}; that is, they do not adhere to the correct religion, even if they claim to be upon a religion, for it is a religion other than the truth. This is because it is either a distorted religion, which Allah never prescribed at all, or an abrogated religion that Allah had prescribed but then changed through the law of Muhammad (ﷺ), so that adhering to it after its abrogation is not permissible. Otherwise, if they do not fulfill this, and do not give the jizyah from their hand while humbled, then their being allowed to remain by paying the jizyah is not permissible, and they shall be fought until they embrace Islam.

The majority of scholars who say that the jizyah is taken only from People of the Book have cited this verse, because Allah mentioned taking the jizyah only from them, and as for others, He mentioned only fighting them until they submit to Islam. This is supported by the fact that the jizyah was taken from the Magians, who are not People of the Book, and because it is widely reported from the Muslims, the Companions and those after them, that they called those they fought to one of three things: either Islam, or paying the jizyah, or the sword, without distinguishing between a People of the Book and anyone else.

{36} Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah﴾, i.e., in Allah's decree and destiny, ﴿is twelve months﴾, which are these well-known months, ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., in His decree of destiny, ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾, and caused their night and day to run their course, and determined their times, dividing them into these twelve months. ﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾, and they are Rajab (al-Fard), Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verse 37:

{37} The nasi' (postponement) is what the people of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) practiced regarding the sacred months. Among their false innovations was that when they found themselves in need of fighting during some of the sacred months, they considered, with their corrupt opinions, that they should preserve the number of the sacred months in which Allah had forbidden fighting, while postponing some of the sacred months or advancing them, and putting in their place from the months of permissibility whatever they wished. When they did this, they made fighting lawful in that month and made the lawful month unlawful. This, as Allah informed about them, is an increase in their disbelief and misguidance, because of the following dangers:
First: They innovated it of their own accord and placed it on the level of the law and religion of Allah, while Allah and His Messenger are free of it.
Second: They reversed the religion, making the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful.
Third: They deceived Allah in their claim and deceived His servants, confused their religion for them, and used deception and trickery in the religion of Allah.
Fourth: Customs that oppose the Shari'ah, if persisted in, cause their ugliness to disappear from souls, and it may be thought that they are good customs, so there resulted from this the error and misguidance that occurred.
For this reason He said: {Through it those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, to conform with the number of what Allah has made sacred} — that is, to agree with them in number — {and so they make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verse 38–39:

{38} Know that much of this noble surah was revealed concerning the expedition of Tabuk, when the Prophet (ﷺ) called upon the Muslims to campaign against the Romans. The weather was hot, provisions were scarce, and life was hard. Some of the Muslims showed such reluctance that it necessitated that God, exalted is He, rebuke them for it and urge them forward. So He, exalted is He, said: {O you who have believed}: Will you not act in accordance with the requirements of faith and the motives of certainty, by hastening to God's command, racing toward His pleasure, striving against His enemies, and supporting your religion? Do you not have minds by which you weigh matters? And which of the two is more worthy of being preferred? Is not the world, from its beginning to its end, of no comparison to the Hereafter? How very short is the span of a human's life in this world, that he should make it the ultimate goal beyond which there is no goal, directing his effort, exertion, concern, and will to nothing beyond this short worldly life, filled with troubles and laden with dangers? By what reasoning did you see fit to prefer it over the Abode of the Hereafter, which gathers every bliss, in which are whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, and in which you will abide eternally? By God, no one who has faith firmly settled in his heart prefers this world over the Hereafter, nor does anyone of sound judgment, nor anyone counted among people of understanding.

{39} Then He threatened them for not going forth, saying: {If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment}: in this world and the Hereafter. Failing to go forth when called upon to do so is among the major sins that necessitate the most severe punishment, because of the grave harms it entails. The one who stays behind has disobeyed God, exalted is He, violated His prohibition, failed to assist in supporting the religion of God, failed to defend the Book of God and His law, and failed to help his Muslim brothers against their enemy, who wants to root them out and obliterate their religion. It may also lead others of weak faith to follow his example, and may even weaken the resolve of those who strive against the enemies of God. Thus it is fitting that one in such a condition be threatened by God with a severe warning. He said: {If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people} who will not be like you, {and they will not harm Him at all}; for He, exalted is He, has undertaken to support His religion and exalt His word. Whether you obey God's command or cast it behind your backs, it makes no difference. {And God is over all things competent}: nothing He wills is beyond His power, and none can overcome Him.

This is the support mentioned in this context, for support is of two types: first, the support of the Muslims when they pursue their enemy, so that Allah fulfills for them what they sought and intended, and they overcome and prevail over their enemy. Thus the religion of Allah is the apparent and dominant one above all other religions, through clear proofs, dazzling signs and a supporting authority. ﴿And Allah is Almighty﴾: no one can overcome Him, and no fugitive escapes Him. ﴿Wise﴾: He places things in their proper places and delays the support of His party until another time that divine wisdom requires.

In this noble verse is the virtue of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, through a distinction not granted to anyone else in this Ummah, namely attaining this exalted merit and this beautiful companionship. The Muslims have agreed that he is the one intended by this noble verse. For this reason they regarded whoever denies Abu Bakr's companionship with the Prophet ﷺ as a disbeliever, because he denies the Qur'an which explicitly affirms it. In it is also the virtue of sakinah (tranquility), and that it is part of Allah's complete favor upon the servant in times of hardship and fear that make hearts tremble, and that it is in proportion to the servant's knowledge of his Lord, his trust in His true promise, and in proportion to his faith and courage. In it also is that sadness may befall the special servants of Allah, the truthful ones; nevertheless, the better course, when it befalls the servant, is to strive to remove it, for it weakens the heart and undermines resolve.

{46} God, exalted is He, explains that among the hypocrites who stayed behind there appeared indications showing that they had never really intended to go out at all, and that the excuses they offered were false. "But Allah was averse to their being sent forth" with you on the campaign (ghazw), "so He held them back" by His decree and destiny, even though He had commanded them and urged them to go out and had made them capable of it; yet in His wisdom He did not will to help them, but rather forsook and restrained them. {47} Then He mentions the wisdom behind this, saying: "Had they gone out among you, they would have increased you only in corruption" (khabal); that is, in loss. Then the Most High explained the manner of distributing the obligatory charities, saying:

{60} God, exalted is He, says: {Indeed, the charities}; that is, the obligatory zakat, as evidenced by the fact that voluntary charity may be given to anyone and is not restricted to any particular person. [That is]: {Indeed, the charities} are for these mentioned categories and no others, because He has restricted them to them. They are eight categories:

The first and second: the poor (fuqara') and the needy (masakin). In this context they are two distinct categories. The poor (faqir) is in greater need than the needy (miskin), because God began with them, and one begins only with the most important and then the next most important. The faqir is defined as one who has nothing, or who has some of his sufficiency but less than half of it. The miskin is one who has half or more of his sufficiency but does not have his full sufficiency, for if he had it he would be rich. They are given from zakat what removes their poverty and neediness.

The third: those employed to collect zakat (al-'amilina 'alayha, the zakat officials). These are everyone who has work or duties in it, such as one who guards it, one who collects it from its owners, a shepherd, one who transports it, a scribe, or the like. They are given on account of their work (ʿamalah), which is a wage for their labour in it.

The fourth: those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum, those whose hearts are inclined toward Islam). The one whose heart is to be reconciled is a leader obeyed among his people, of whom one hopes for his conversion to Islam, or whose evil is feared, or through whose gift the strength of his faith or the conversion of his peers is hoped for, or who collects zakat from those who refuse to give it. He is given what achieves the reconciliation and the public interest.

The fifth: the captives (al-riqab), namely the mukatabun (slaves contracted to buy their freedom) who have purchased themselves from their masters. They strive to earn what will free them, and so they are assisted from zakat in that. The freeing of a Muslim captive held by the disbelievers is included in this, and is even more deserving. It is also permissible to free slaves independently from this category, since it falls under His words: {and for the captives}.

The sixth: the debtors (al-gharimun), who are of two kinds. One: those who are in debt for the reconciliation of people (li-islah dhat al-bayn), which is when there is evil and strife between two groups of people, and a man intervenes to reconcile them with money that he spends on one of them or on all of them. He is given a share of zakat so that this will encourage him and strengthen his resolve, and he is given even if he is rich. The second: one who incurred debt for himself and then became unable to pay; he is given what will settle his debt.

The seventh: those who fight in the way of God (fi sabil Allah), namely volunteer fighters who have no regular register (diwan). They are given from zakat what helps them in their fighting, such as the price of weapons or a mount, or provision for themselves and their dependants, so that they may devote themselves to jihad and their hearts be at ease. Many jurists have said: if one capable of earning a living devotes himself to seeking knowledge, he is given from zakat, because knowledge falls within jihad in the way of God. They also said: it is permissible to give from it to a poor person for the obligatory Hajj. But there is room for consideration in this.

The eighth: the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), who is a stranger cut off from his means in a land other than his own, and so is given from zakat what will bring him to his homeland.

These are the eight categories to whom zakat is given, and to them alone. {An obligation from God}: He prescribed it and decreed it in accordance with His knowledge and wisdom, {and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise}.

Know that these eight categories return to two matters: first, those who are given for their own need and benefit, such as the poor, the needy and the like; second, those who are given because of the need for them and the benefit Islam derives from them.

God therefore made this portion obligatory in the wealth of the rich to meet the particular and general needs of Islam and the Muslims. Had the rich given the zakat of their wealth in the lawful manner, no poor person among the Muslims would remain, and there would be sufficient wealth to secure the frontiers, to wage jihad against the disbelievers with it, and to achieve all the religious interests.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 69–70:

{69–70} He, exalted is He, says, warning the hypocrites that there may befall them what befell those before them of the denying nations: {the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud, and the people of Abraham, and the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities}, meaning the towns of the people of Lot. They denied it, and so there befell them what Allah has related to us. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 73–74:

{73} The Exalted says to His Prophet (ﷺ): {O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites}; i.e., exert yourself in striving against them, and be harsh with them where the situation calls for harshness. This striving (jihad) includes striving by hand and striving by proof and tongue. Whoever among them openly wages war is to be fought with the hand, the tongue, the sword and the spear. Whoever submits to Islam through a dhimma (protected status) or a covenant is to be striven against through proof and argument, and the excellence of Islam and the evils of shirk and disbelief are to be made clear to him. This is what awaits them in this world. {And} as for the Hereafter, {their refuge is Hell}; i.e., their abode from which they will never leave, {and wretched is the destination}.

{74} {They swear by Allah that they did not say [it], but they did say the word of disbelief}; i.e., when they said a statement like the statement of one of them: {Surely the mightier will expel therefrom the weaker}, and the words that one of them spoke after another in mockery of the religion and of the Messenger. When it reached them that the Prophet (ﷺ) had been informed of something of that, they came to him swearing by Allah that they had not said it. Allah, the Exalted, refuted them, saying: {They did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam}. Their earlier Islam, although its apparent meaning is that it removed them from the circle of disbelief, their final statement nullifies their Islam and returns them to disbelief. {And they plotted what they could not attain}: this was when they plotted to assassinate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the Battle of Tabuk, so Allah related their news to him, and he commanded those who would repel them from their intent. {And} the situation is that they {found fault} and disparaged the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only {because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty}, after they had been poor and needy. This is among the most astonishing things: that they should belittle the one who was the cause of their being brought out of darkness into light, and who enriched them after poverty! Is his right over them anything other than that they should honor him, believe in him, and revere him? [Thus the call of religion and the call of human dignity converge.] Then He offered them repentance, saying: {So if they repent, it is better for them}; because repentance is the foundation of happiness in this world and the Hereafter. {But if they turn away}: from repentance and returning to Allah, {Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter}: in this world by the distress, grief and sorrow that will befall them over Allah's support of His religion and the honoring of His Prophet, and their failure to attain what they sought; and in the Hereafter, in the punishment of the Blaze. {And they will have no protector on earth}: one who manages their affairs and obtains what they want, {nor any helper}: one who repels what they dislike. When they are cut off from the guardianship of Allah, the Exalted, there await them all kinds of evil, loss, misery and deprivation.

Whoever submits to Islam through a dhimma (protected status) or a covenant is to be striven against through proof and argument, and the excellence of Islam and the evils of shirk and disbelief are to be made clear to him. This is what awaits them in this world. {And} as for the Hereafter, {their refuge is Hell}; i.e., their abode from which they will never leave, {and wretched is the destination}.

{74} {They swear by Allah that they did not say [it], but they did say the word of disbelief}; i.e., when they said a statement like the statement of one of them: {Surely the mightier will expel therefrom the weaker}, and the words that one of them spoke after another in mockery of the religion and of the Messenger. {75} That is: among these hypocrites are some who gave Allah their covenant and pledge: {If He gives us of His bounty}, [of worldly wealth], by spreading it out for us and widening it, {we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous}: we will keep the ties of kinship, host the guest, help with the calamities of right, and do good and righteous deeds.

He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him to supplicate to Allah that He give him of His bounty, and that if He gave him, he would surely give charity, keep the ties of kinship, and help with the calamities of right. The Prophet (ﷺ) missed him and was informed of his condition, so he sent someone to collect the charity from its people. They passed by Tha'labah, and he said: "This is nothing but jizyah, this is nothing but the sister of jizyah." When he did not give them anything, they came and informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of this, and he said: "Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah!" three times. When these verses were revealed concerning him and those like him, some of his relatives took them to him and conveyed them to him, so he came with his zakat, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not accept it. Then he brought it to Abu Bakr after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), but he did not accept it. Then he brought it after Abu Bakr to 'Umar, but he did not accept it. It is said that he died during the time of 'Uthman.

{79} This too is among the shameful deeds of the hypocrites. May God curse them: they never left any matter of Islam and the Muslims without speaking about it, and whenever they found something to say, they spoke and slandered out of rebelliousness and hostility. Among them: their slander of the believers because of their faith, which is disbelief in God and hatred of the religion.

Among them: that fault-finding (lamz) is forbidden, indeed it is among the major sins in worldly matters; as for fault-finding in matters of obedience, it is more and more reprehensible.

Among them: that whoever obeys God and volunteers some good quality, it is fitting to help and encourage him in his deed, while these people intended to discourage him by what they said about him and the criticism they leveled at him.

Among them: that their judgment upon one who spent much wealth as being a showoff is a gross error and a judgment on the unseen and a throwing of guesses; and what evil is greater than this?!

Among them: that their saying to the owner of the small charity, "God is free of need from this man's charity!", is a statement whose intent is false; for God is free of need from the charity of the one who gives little or much, indeed He is free of need from all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, but He commanded the servants with what they are in need of; so although God is free of need from it, they are in need of it: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 81–83:

{81} He, exalted is He, says, explaining the boasting of the hypocrites over their staying behind and their indifference about it, which indicates the absence of faith and the choice of disbelief over belief: {Those who were left behind rejoiced in their staying behind, against the Messenger of Allah}. This is an addition beyond mere staying behind, for this is a forbidden staying behind, together with an increase in contentment with committing the act of disobedience and boasting about it. {And they disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah}. This is in contrast to the believers, who, when they stay behind even due to an excuse, grieve over their staying behind and feel the utmost regret, and they love to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, because of the faith in their hearts, and they hope for the bounty, kindness, benevolence and generosity of Allah. {And they said}, i.e., the hypocrites: {Do not go forth in the heat}, i.e., they said: indeed, going forth is a hardship for us because of the heat. So they preferred a brief, fleeting comfort over the complete, everlasting comfort, and they were wary of the heat from which shade protects and which the cool of morning and evening removes, over the intense heat whose degree cannot be measured, namely the blazing Fire. For this reason He said: {Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood}.

{82} When they preferred what perishes over what endures, and when they fled from a light, fleeting hardship to a severe, lasting hardship, He, exalted is He, said: {So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much}, i.e., let them enjoy themselves in this transient abode, rejoice in its pleasures, and amuse themselves with its play; for they will weep much in a painful punishment. {As recompense for what they used to earn}: of disbelief, hypocrisy, and not submitting to the commands of their Lord.

{83} {So if Allah returns you to a group of them}: namely those who stayed behind without an excuse and did not grieve over their staying behind. {And they ask your permission to go out}: for other than this expedition, when they see it is easy. {Then say}, as a punishment to them: {You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me. Indeed, you were satisfied with staying behind the first time, so sit [now] with those who remain behind}. And this is as He, exalted is He, said: {And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, as they did not believe in it the first time}. For the one who is sluggish and stays behind from what he was commanded, when the opportunity presents itself, will not be granted success in it afterward, and it will be made impossible for him to reach it. There is also in this a rebuke to them; for when it is established among the Muslims that these people are among those prevented from going out to jihad because of their disobedience, that becomes a reproach to them, a stigma upon them, and a deterrent that anyone should do as they did.

This third state is the one Allah commanded regarding the hypocrites, and for this reason He said: {They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, that you may turn away from them, so turn away from them}; i.e., do not rebuke them, nor flog them, nor kill them. {Indeed, they are an abomination}; i.e., they are filth and corrupt, not people who deserve to be cared about, and rebuke and punishment are of no benefit regarding them. {And} Hell is sufficient as their punishment {as recompense for what they used to earn}.

{96} His saying: {They swear to you that you may be pleased with them}; i.e., they also have this other aim from you beyond mere turning away, rather they love that you be pleased with them as if they had done nothing. {But if you should be pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people}; i.e., it is not fitting for you, O believers, to be pleased with those with whom Allah is not pleased; rather you must agree with your Lord in His pleasure and His anger. Consider how He said: {Indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people}, and did not say: "Indeed, Allah is not pleased with them." This indicates that the door of repentance is open, and that whenever they repent, whether they or others, Allah accepts their repentance and is pleased with them. But as long as they remain defiantly disobedient, Allah is not pleased with them, due to the existence of the barrier to His pleasure, which is their departure from what Allah has approved for them of faith and obedience to what displeases Him of polytheism, hypocrisy and sins.

The summary of what Allah has mentioned is that the hypocrites who stay behind from jihad without an excuse, when they make excuses to the believers and claim that they have excuses for their staying behind, the hypocrites intend by this that you turn away from them, be pleased with them, and accept their excuse. As for accepting their excuse and being pleased with them, that is not out of love or honor for them. As for turning away from them, the believers turn away from them as they turn away from base and abominable matters.

In these verses there is an affirmation of speech for Allah, the Exalted, in His saying: {Allah has already informed us of your news}, and an affirmation of voluntary actions of Allah that occur by His will and power, both in this and in His saying: {And Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger}; He informed that He will see it after it occurs. And in them is an affirmation of Allah's pleasure with the good-doers, and of His anger and wrath toward the defiantly disobedient.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 97–99:

{97} He, exalted is He, says: {The Bedouins}, who are the inhabitants of the desert and the wilderness, {are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy}, than the settled folk, among whom there is disbelief and hypocrisy, and that is for many reasons. Among them: they are far from knowledge of the religious laws, the acts of worship and the rulings; so they are more inclined, {and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger}, of the foundations of faith and the rulings of commands and prohibitions. Unlike the settled folk, who are closer to knowing the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger, so that through this knowledge good conceptions and wills toward goodness arise in them, which those in the desert do not know. Among them there is also a refinement of disposition and a readiness to answer the call that the desert-dwellers lack. They also sit with the people of faith and mix with them more than the desert-dwellers do; therefore they are more inclined to goodness than the desert-dwellers, even though there are disbelievers and hypocrites both in the desert and among the settled folk; the disbelief and hypocrisy in the desert are more intense and severe than in the settled areas.

{98} Among this is that the Bedouins are more greedy for wealth and more miserly with it. Among them is the one who {takes what he spends}, from zakat and spending in the way of Allah and other things, {as a loss}; that is, he regards it as a loss and a deficiency, does not expect a reward for it, does not seek thereby the Face of Allah, and pays it only with reluctance. {And they wait for misfortunes to befall you}; that is, from their enmity toward the believers and their hatred of them, they wish for and await the vicissitudes of time and the calamities of the age against them; and this will be reflected back upon them. For them is {the evil turn of fortune}. As for the believers, for them is the good turn of fortune over their enemies, and for them is the good final outcome. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows the intentions of the servants and what actions proceed from them, whether sincere or otherwise.

{99} Not all the Bedouins are blameworthy; rather, among them are those {who believe in Allah and the Last Day}: so by that they are safe from disbelief and hypocrisy, and act in accordance with the requirements of faith, {and take what they spend as means of nearness to Allah}; that is, they reckon their spending and intend thereby the Face of Allah and nearness to Him, {and as [a means to obtain] the prayers of the Messenger}; that is, his supplication for them and his blessing upon them. Allah, the Exalted, said, explaining the benefit of the Messenger's prayers: {Unquestionably, they are a means of nearness for them}: bringing them near to Allah, increasing their wealth, and bestowing blessing upon it. {Allah will admit them to His mercy}: among the group of His righteous servants. Indeed He is {Forgiving and Merciful}: He forgives great sins for whoever repents to Him, extends His mercy, which encompasses all things, to His servants in general, and specially favors His believing servants with a mercy by which He enables them to do good, protects them from transgressions, and bestows upon them abundant kinds of reward.

In this verse there is evidence that the Bedouins are like the settled folk: among them are the praiseworthy and among them the blameworthy. Allah did not blame them merely for being Bedouin or living in the desert; rather He blamed them for abandoning Allah's commands, and that they are prone to that.

Among its lessons: disbelief and hypocrisy increase, decrease, grow stronger and lighten according to circumstances.

Among them: the virtue of knowledge, and that one who lacks it is closer to evil than one who possesses it; for Allah blamed the Bedouins, informed that they are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy, mentioned the cause that necessitates this, and that they are more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger.

Among them: that beneficial knowledge, which is the most beneficial of sciences, is knowledge of the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger, of the foundations and branches of religion; such as knowing the limits of faith, Islam, excellence (ihsan), piety, success, obedience, righteousness, kinship, benevolence, disbelief, hypocrisy, wickedness, disobedience, fornication, wine, usury and the like; for in knowing them one is enabled to perform them if they are commanded, or to abandon them if they are forbidden, and to enjoin them or forbid them.

Among them: that the believer should discharge what is due upon him of rights, with an open breast and a tranquil soul, and be eager that it be a gain and not a loss.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verse 102–103:

{102} He, exalted is He, says: {And others} – from among those in Medina and around it, and indeed from among all the Islamic lands – {have acknowledged their sins}; that is, they admitted them, regretted them, strove in repentance from them and in purifying themselves from their defilements. {They mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil}. A deed is not righteous unless the servant possesses the root of tawhid (monotheism) and faith, which removes one from disbelief and polytheism, and which is a condition for every righteous deed. These people mixed righteous deeds with evil deeds: transgressing against some of the prohibitions and falling short in some of the obligations, while acknowledging that and hoping that Allah would forgive them. Regarding these, {it is hoped that Allah will accept their repentance}. His accepting repentance from His servant is of two kinds. The first is granting them the success to repent. The second is accepting it after it has occurred from them. {Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful}; that is, He has the attributes of forgiveness and mercy, which no creature is free of, indeed without which neither the upper nor the lower world could endure. For if Allah were to take people to account for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon its surface a single creature that moves. {Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Oft-Forgiving.} Among His forgiveness is that those who have been excessive against themselves, who have spent their lives in evil deeds, if they repent to Him and turn back to Him, even shortly before their death, He pardons them and overlooks their evil deeds. This verse indicates that the one who mixes deeds, acknowledges, and regrets, but has not made a sincere repentance, is between fear and hope, and he is nearer to safety. As for the one who mixes deeds but does not acknowledge, does not regret what has passed, and continues persisting in sins, he is to be feared with the greatest fear.

{103} Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger, and to whoever stands in his position, commanding him with what purifies the believers and completes their faith: {Take from their wealth a charity}, which is the obligatory zakah, {by which you purify them and cause them to grow}; that is, purify them from sins and base character, {and cause them to grow}; that is, develop them, increase their good character and righteous deeds, increase their reward in this world and the Hereafter, and make their wealth grow. {And pray for them}; that is, supplicate for them – for the believers in general and in particular – when they give you the zakah of their wealth. {Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them}; that is, a tranquility for their hearts and a joy for them. {And Allah is Hearing}, of your supplication, hearing with acceptance and response. {Knowing}, of the states of the servants and their intentions, so He will reward each worker according to his deed and in proportion to his intention. The Prophet (ﷺ) would comply with the command of Allah, command the people to give charity, and send his agents to collect it; when someone brought him his charity, he would supplicate for him and bless him.

In this verse is an indication of the obligation of zakah on all kinds of wealth, and this applies when the wealth is clearly for trade, for such wealth is that which grows and by which gain is made; so it is just that one should aid the poor from it by paying what Allah has made obligatory in it of zakah. As for wealth other than trade goods: if the wealth is of a growing kind, such as grains, fruits, and livestock kept for growth, milk, and breeding, zakah is obligatory on them; otherwise, it is not obligatory on them, because if they are held for personal use, they are not in the position of wealth that a person ordinarily acquires as property to be invested and from which financial aims are sought; rather, they have been diverted from being wealth by personal use and the like.

Also in it: a servant cannot purify himself and cause himself to grow until he pays the zakah of his wealth, and nothing expiates it except paying it, because zakah and purification depend upon its payment.

Also in it: the recommendation that the leader, or his deputy, supplicate for the one who has paid his zakah, asking for blessing, and that this should be done aloud, so that the giver hears it and is comforted by it.

It is understood from the meaning that one should bring joy to the believer through gentle speech, supplication for him, and the like, which bring tranquility and calm to his heart. [And that one should encourage whoever spends and does a righteous deed by supplicating for him, praising him, and the like.]

{104} That is: Do they not know the vastness of Allah's mercy and the generality of His generosity, and that He {accepts repentance from His servants}: from those who repent of any sin whatsoever? {106} That is: {And others} from among those who stayed behind are deferred {until God's command comes: either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness}. So when His wisdom requires that He forgive them and turn to them, He forgives them and turns to them. And if His wisdom requires that He forsake them and not grant them success in repentance, He does that.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verse 107–110:

{107} There were some hypocrites from the people of Quba who took a mosque beside the mosque of Quba, intending by it harm and enmity between the believers, and preparing it for those whom they hoped would wage war against Allah and His Messenger, so that it would be a fortress for them when they needed it. So Allah, exalted is He, exposed their disgrace and revealed their secret, and said: {And those who took a mosque for harm}; that is, to harm the believers and their mosque in which they gathered, {and disbelief}; that is, their aim in it is disbelief, when others intend faith, {and division among the believers}; that is, to split them, scatter them and cause them to differ, {and in preparation for one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before}; that is, in preparation (irsad) for aiding those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, whose hostility had already preceded and whose enmity had grown severe. This refers to Abu 'Amir al-Rahib (the monk), who was from the people of Madinah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived and migrated to Madinah, he disbelieved in him. He had been a devotee in the Jahiliyyah, so he went to the polytheists seeking their help in fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he did not achieve his aim among them, he went to Caesar, claiming that he would support him. The accursed one died on the way. He had been in agreement and collusion with the hypocrites, and among what they prepared for him was the mosque of harm. {111} He, the Exalted, reports a true report and promises a true promise, of a great exchange and a weighty transaction: that He has "purchased" (ishtara), by His noble Self, "from the believers their souls and their wealth" (the souls and wealth are the price and the goods sold), "in return for which they shall have Paradise" (al-Jannah), in which is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, of all kinds of pleasures, joys, delights, beautiful wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-hisan) and elegant dwellings. The form of the contract and the exchange is that they give up to God their souls and their wealth in striving against His enemies, to raise high His word and to manifest His religion. So they fight "in the way of God; they kill and are killed." This contract and exchange has been issued by God, confirmed with every kind of emphasis, "a promise binding upon Him in truth, in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an" (these are the most noble of the Books that have reached the world, the highest and most complete of them, brought by the most complete of the Messengers, the possessors of firm resolve (ulu al-azm), and all of them agree upon this true promise). "And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your exchange which you have made" (O believers, who fulfil what God has promised you), that is: so that you may rejoice in it, and that some of you may give glad tidings to others and urge one another on. "That is the supreme triumph" (al-fawz al-azim), than which there is no greater or more glorious triumph, because it includes everlasting happiness, enduring bliss, and the good pleasure of God, which is greater than the bliss of the Gardens.

If you wish to know the value of this transaction, then look at the Purchaser: who is He? He is God, majestic in His majesty. Look at the return, which is the greatest and most glorious of returns: the Gardens of Bliss. Look at the price given for it, which is the soul and the wealth, the most beloved of things to a human being. Look at the one through whose hands this contract was conducted, who is the most noble of the Messengers. And by what Book was it inscribed? They are the great Books of God, sent down upon the best of creation.

{112} It is as if it were said: Who are the believers to whom God gives the good tidings of entry into the Gardens and the attainment of honours? He said: They are: {those who repent} (al-tā'ibūn), i.e., those who constantly persist in repentance at all times from all misdeeds. {Those who worship} (al-'ābidūn), i.e., those characterised by servitude to God and by persistence in His obedience, through performing the obligatory and recommended acts at all times; by this a servant becomes one of the worshippers. {Those who praise} (al-ḥāmidūn) God in times of ease and hardship, in prosperity and adversity, acknowledging the favours of God upon them, both apparent and hidden, extolling God for them and remembering Him in the hours of the night and the hours of the day. {Those who travel} (al-sā'iḥūn): sayaḥa (travel/wandering) has been interpreted as fasting, or as travelling in pursuit of knowledge; and it has been interpreted as the wandering of the heart in knowing God, loving Him and turning to Him constantly. The correct view is that what is meant by sayaḥa is travel in acts of devotion, such as the Ḥajj, the 'Umrah, jihad, seeking knowledge, maintaining ties of kinship, and the like. {Those who bow and prostrate} (al-rāki'ūn al-sājidūn), i.e., those who frequently perform prayer, which includes bowing and prostration. {Those who enjoin what is good} (al-āmirūn bi'l-ma'rūf): this includes all obligatory and recommended acts. {And those who forbid what is evil} (al-nāhūn 'an al-munkar): this is everything that God and His Messenger have forbidden. {And those who guard the limits of God} (al-ḥāfiẓūn li-ḥudūd Allāh): by their learning the limits of what God has sent down to His Messenger, and what falls under the commands, prohibitions and rulings, and what does not, and by their adherence to them in action and abstention. {And give good tidings to the believers}: He did not mention what they are given good tidings of, so that it may encompass all that is ordained for faith of reward in this world, in religion and in the Hereafter. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verses 117–118:

{117} He, exalted is He, informs that, from His kindness and benevolence, {He turned in forgiveness to the Prophet}, Muhammad (ﷺ), {and the Muhajirun and the Ansar}. So He forgave them their slips, multiplied their good deeds for them, and elevated them to the highest ranks. This was because of their undertaking of difficult and arduous tasks. Therefore He said: {who followed him in the hour of hardship}; that is, they went out with him to fight the enemy in the expedition of Tabuk, which was in severe heat, with a shortage of provisions and mounts, and a large enemy, all of which called for staying behind. Yet they sought help from God Most High and carried out that duty, {after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved}; that is, their hearts were about to turn and incline toward ease and rest. But God steadied them, supported them, and strengthened them.

Swerving of the heart (zaygh al-qalb) is its deviation from the straight path. If the deviation is in the foundation of the religion, it is disbelief; if it is in its legislated rulings, it is according to the ruling from which one has swerved: either one falls short in performing it, or performs it in a manner other than the legislated way. His words {then He turned to them}; that is, He accepted their repentance. {Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful}: from His kindness and mercy is that He bestowed upon them repentance, accepted it from them, and made them steadfast in it.

{118} {And} likewise, God {turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind}: from going out with the Muslims in that expedition. They were Ka'b ibn Malik and his two companions, and their story is well known and famous in the Sahihs and the Sunan. {Until when}: they grieved greatly, {the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness}; that is, despite its spaciousness and breadth, {and their souls became constricted for them}: which are dearer to them than everything else. So the wide expanse and the beloved became narrow for them, something whose custom does not involve being constricted by it. This could only come from a distressing matter that reached such severity and hardship that it cannot be described. This was because they had placed the pleasure of God and the pleasure of His Messenger above everything. {And they thought that there is no refuge from God except in Him}; that is, they became certain and recognized from their condition that none can deliver from calamities and to whom one resorts except God alone, without partner. Thus their attachment to created beings ceased, they clung to God their Lord, and fled from Him to Him. They remained in this hardship for about fifty nights. {Then He turned to them}; that is, He permitted their repentance and granted them success in it, {so that they might repent}; that is, so that it would occur from them, and God would then turn to them in forgiveness. {Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance}; that is, He is abundant in repentance, pardon, and forgiveness of slips and shortcomings, {the Merciful}: His attribute is great mercy that continually descends upon the servants at every time and moment, in every instant, by which their religious and worldly affairs are sustained.

In these verses is evidence that God's turning in forgiveness toward the servant is the most exalted goal and the highest end, for God made it the final station of His elite servants and bestowed it upon them when they performed deeds that He loves and is pleased with.

From them: God's kindness toward them and His steadying them in their faith amid hardships and distressing calamities.

From them: that arduous worship upon the self has a merit and distinction that others lack, and the greater the hardship, the greater the reward.

From them: that God's turning in forgiveness toward His servant is in proportion to his regret and intense remorse, and that whoever is indifferent to sin and feels no discomfort when committing it, his repentance is flawed, even if he claims it is accepted.

From them: that a sign of goodness and the removal of hardship is when the heart becomes fully attached to God Most High and cut off from created beings.

From them: that among God's kindness to the three is that He marked them with a label that is no shame upon them, saying: {were left behind}; indicating that the believers left them behind, or that they were left behind by the one who decided whether to accept their excuse or reject it, and that their staying behind was not out of aversion to good. For this reason He did not say "they stayed behind."

From them: that God Most High bestowed upon them truthfulness, and for this reason He commanded following their example, saying:

{120} Allah the Exalted urges the people of Madinah, the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those of the Bedouins around them who embraced Islam and whose Islam was good: ﴿It was not for the people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾; that is, it is not fitting for them to do so, nor does it suit their circumstances. ﴿Nor to prefer themselves over his self﴾: over his noble and pure self, in regard to remaining and comfort and rest. Rather, the Prophet is more entitled to the believers than they are to themselves. Every Muslim must ransom the Prophet (ﷺ) with his own self and give him precedence over it. The sign of honouring the Messenger, loving him, and having complete faith in him is that they do not stay behind him. Then he mentioned the reward that motivates going out, saying: ﴿That is because they﴾; that is, the strivers in the way of Allah, ﴿no thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger befalls them in the way of Allah﴾; that is, weariness and hardship, ﴿nor hunger in the way of Allah﴾; that is, famine, ﴿nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers﴾, by entering their lands and seizing their homelands, ﴿nor do they inflict on an enemy any infliction﴾, such as defeating an army or a detachment, or taking spoils of wealth, ﴿except that a righteous deed is written for them thereby﴾, because these are effects arising from their deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good﴾: those who did good in hastening to the command of Allah and standing by what is incumbent upon them of His right and the rights of His creatures. These deeds are, then, effects of the effects of their work.

{121} Then he said: ﴿Nor do they spend any expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross a valley﴾ in their going to their enemy, ﴿except that it is written for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾; and among that are these deeds when they are sincere to Allah in them and give sincere counsel in them.

In these verses there is the strongest encouragement and enticement of souls to go forth to striving in the way of Allah, and to seek reward from Allah for the hardships that befall them therein, and that this brings them elevation of ranks, and that the effects that result from a servant's deed carry a great reward for him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 9, verse 122:

{122} The Exalted says, alerting His believing servants to what is fitting for them: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾; that is, all together to fight their enemy, for that would cause them hardship and cause many other interests to be lost. ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾; that is, from every region, tribe and clan, ﴿a party﴾ whereby sufficiency and the objective are achieved. That would be more appropriate.

Then He pointed out that in the residing of those among them who remain, and in their not going forth, there are interests which would be lost had they gone forth. So He said: ﴿that they may gain understanding (yatafaqqahu) in the religion﴾; that is, those who stay behind, ﴿and that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾; that is, so that they may learn the religious knowledge, know its meanings, comprehend its secrets, teach others, and warn their people when they return to them.

In this is the virtue of knowledge, especially understanding (fiqh) of the religion, and that it is among the most important matters; and that whoever learns a branch of knowledge must spread it and disseminate it among the servants and advise them with it, for the spread of knowledge from the scholar is part of its blessing and its reward, which grows. As for the scholar confining himself to himself, not calling to the way of God with wisdom and fair admonition, and leaving off teaching the ignorant what they do not know, what benefit has the Muslims gained from him? And what result has come from his knowledge? Its end is that he dies and his knowledge and its fruit die with him, and this is the utmost deprivation for one whom God has given knowledge and granted understanding.

In this verse there is also a guidance, instruction and subtle alert to an important benefit: that the Muslims should prepare for each of their general interests someone who will undertake it, devote his time to it, strive in it, and not turn to anything else, so that their interests may be upheld and their benefits completed, and so that the direction of all of them and the ultimate goal of what they aim at may be one single aim, namely the upholding of the interest of their religion and their worldly life, even if the paths diverge and the sources multiply. The works are varied, but the aim is one, and this is part of the general wisdom that is beneficial in all matters.

{123} This is another guidance: after He instructed them regarding the arrangement of those who engage in fighting, He instructed them to begin with the nearest of the disbelievers and then the next nearest, and to be firm against them, and to be steadfast, courageous and resolute in battle. ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing.﴾ That is: let it be known to you that aid from Allah descends in proportion to taqwa (God-consciousness and piety). So hold fast to the fear of Allah, and He will help you and grant you victory over your enemy. This generality in His words ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you﴾ is restricted to the case where the benefit lies in fighting others than those nearest to us, and the kinds of benefit are very numerous.

{124} Says the Exalted, explaining the condition of the hypocrites and the believers when the Qur'an is revealed, and the difference between the two groups, so He says: {And whenever a surah is sent down}: in it are commands, prohibitions, information about Himself—may He be glorified—and about unseen matters, and an exhortation to jihad. {Among them are some who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?"}; that is: the question arose from whoever among the two groups had received faith through it. The Exalted says, explaining the actual state: {As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith}: through knowledge of it, understanding it, believing in it, acting upon it, desiring to do good, and refraining from doing evil. {And they rejoice}; that is: some of them give good news to others of what Allah has bestowed upon them of His signs and of the success in understanding them and acting upon them. This indicates the expansion of their hearts toward the signs of Allah, the tranquility of their hearts, and the swiftness of their submission to what it urges them to.

{125} {And as for those in whose hearts is a disease}; that is: doubt and hypocrisy, {it has increased them in filth upon their filth}; that is: disease added to their disease, and doubt added to their doubt; because they disbelieved in it, opposed it, and turned away from it, their disease increased by that, and it led them to destruction, and a seal was placed upon their hearts, until {they died while they were disbelievers}. This is a punishment for them, because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and disobeyed His Messenger, so He caused them to have hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him.

{126} The Exalted says, rebuking them for persisting in the disbelief and hypocrisy they are upon: {Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice}: by the calamities and illnesses that befall them, and by the divine commands through which they are tried, {then they do not repent}: from the evil they are upon, {nor do they remember}: what would benefit them so that they might do it, or what would harm them so that they might abandon it. Allah tests them, as is His way with all nations, with adversity and ease, and with commands and prohibitions, so that they might return to Him; yet they do not repent, nor do they remember.

These verses are evidence that faith increases and decreases, and that the believer should examine his faith, attend to it, renew it, and cultivate it, so that he may always be ascending.

This is a punishment for them, because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and disobeyed His Messenger, so He caused them to have hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him.

{126} The Exalted says, rebuking them for persisting in the disbelief and hypocrisy they are upon: {Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice}: by the calamities and illnesses that befall them, and by the divine commands through which they are tried, {then they do not repent}: from the evil they are upon, {nor do they remember}: what would benefit them so that they might do it, or what would harm them so that they might abandon it. Allah tests them, as is His way with all nations, with adversity and ease, and with commands and prohibitions, so that they might return to Him; yet they do not repent, nor do they remember.

These verses are evidence that faith increases and decreases, and that the believer should examine his faith, attend to it, renew it, and cultivate it, so that he may always be ascending.

And His saying:

{128} Exalted is He, Who bestows His favour upon His believing servants by sending among them the unlettered Prophet, who is one of themselves: they know his circumstances, they are able to take from him, and they do not disdain to submit to him, while he - may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him - is in the utmost sincerity toward them and striving for their welfare. {It grieves him what you suffer}; i.e., the matter that burdens you and causes you hardship burdens him. {Ardent over you}: he loves good for you, strives with all his effort to bring it to you, is eager to guide you to faith, and dislikes evil for you, striving with all his effort to turn you away from it. {To the believers, compassionate and merciful}; i.e., exceedingly tender and merciful toward them, more merciful to them than their own parents. Therefore his right takes precedence over all the rights of creation, and it is obligatory upon the Ummah to believe in him, to exalt him, to honour him, and to support him.

{129} {But if} they turn away, then that is their own loss and their own failure to be guided; and if they {turn away} from faith and action, then proceed upon your way, do not waver in your call, and say: {Allah is sufficient for me}; i.e., Allah suffices me in everything that concerns me. {There is no deity except Him}; i.e., there is no worshipped one in truth besides Him. {Upon Him I have relied}; i.e., I have depended upon Him and trusted in Him to bring what benefits and to ward off what harms. {And He is the Lord of the Great Throne}: the Throne being the greatest of created things. And if He is the Lord of the Great Throne, which encompasses all creation, then He is all the more the Lord of what is beneath it.

The tafsir of Surat at-Tawbah is completed by the help and grace of Allah. To Allah belongs all praise, first and last, outward and inward.
